label: copy-phase echoed "s" input, strongest when the next output is "m"
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, never in the original or delimiter phases. 97% of activation mass is on steps where the fed-back input is "s" (the rest is on "m"). Only about 6% of copy-phase "s" inputs fire, so the feature is selective. The strongest modulator is the token being output next: when it is "m" (an "s m" bigram in the original) the feature is strongest, with 63% of mass and 78% of top-quartile activations. Next outputs "1", "s", "x" and "d" give weaker firing. It is also stronger at mid-sequence recall positions (recall_idx 3-4, i.e. s at original position 2-3, e.g. "a j s m m" -> 3.5) and weak or silent when s is at original position 0-1 or is the last token. It does not fire on "s" in the original phase or on first occurrences of a token. Precision of the s-then-m rule is about 0.63; recall is incomplete because weaker activations come from s followed by other tokens.
